findings.problem: The Big Idea skips Isaiah 55:4-5 entirely: David made a witness to the nations and a leader and commander of the peoples, nations who do not know them running to them, and the LORD bestowing glory on them. Line 3 stops at David (Isa 55:3) and line 4 jumps to Isaiah 55:6-7, so the passage's turn outward to the nations is missing.

rule.text: It covers the whole passage, including any included parable or sermon.

findings.problem: The lines mostly walk through the verses in order, each with its own reference (55:1, 55:2, 55:3, 55:6-7, 55:8-9, 55:10-11, 55:12-13), so it reads as a condensed retelling rather than a summary of what the passage means. Apart from short framings ('What He offers is free', 'The real feast is listening to Him'), it rarely says what the whole invitation means for the baker, beyond the closing 'just COME'.

rule.text: A real summary of what the passage means, not a retelling of the verses.

findings.problem: The quote "listen, so that your soul may live," changes the BSB punctuation. Isaiah 55:3 reads 'listen, so that your soul may live.' with a period, not a comma.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The quote "Seek the LORD while He may be found." ends with a period. Isaiah 55:6 has a semicolon there: 'Seek the LORD while He may be found;'.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: 'Anyone who turns back, even the wicked man, our God will freely pardon' goes further than Isaiah 55:7. The verse is about the wicked man and the unrighteous man forsaking his way and his thoughts and returning to the LORD. It doesn't say 'anyone', and 'even' presents the wicked man as the extreme case, which the text doesn't do. It also leaves out the forsaking his way and thoughts that comes with the return.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
